name: AMASS: Archive of Motion Capture as Surface Shapes
description: AMASS is a large and varied database of human motion that unifies 15 different optical marker-based mocap datasets by representing them within a common framework and parameterization using the SMPL body model. It contains more than 40 hours of motion data, spanning over 300 subjects, more than 11000 motions. The dataset includes SMPL 3D shape parameters, DMPL soft tissue coefficients, and full SMPL pose parameters including hand articulations.
creator: Naureen Mahmood, Nima Ghorbani, Nikolaus F. Troje, Gerard Pons-Moll, Michael J. Black
publisher: MPI for Intelligent Systems, Meshcapade GmbH, York University, MPI for Informatics
citeAs: Mahmood, N., Ghorbani, N., Troje, N. F., Pons-Moll, G., & Black, M. J. (2019). AMASS: Archive of Motion Capture as Surface Shapes.
rai:dataCollection: AMASS unifies 15 existing optical marker-based motion capture datasets. Publicly available datasets were downloaded from the internet. Several other datasets were obtained privately or recorded by the authors (Dancers, Transitions, BioMotionLab and SSM). The SSM dataset was recorded using an OptiTrack motion capture system (24 Optitrack Prime 17W optical mocap cameras) synchronized with a 3dMD 4D body scanning system capable of capturing high-resolution 3D scans at 60 frames per second. Each subject was fitted with 67 reflective mocap markers. The 4D system uses 22 pairs of stereo cameras, 22 color cameras and 34 speckle projectors and arrays of white-light LED panels.
rai:dataCollectionType: Physical data collection, Secondary Data analysis, Web Scraping
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: During a mocap session, markers may get occluded by the body due to pose. If multiple markers of a particular body part are occluded simultaneously, the optimization may result in unreliable and implausible poses. A coefficient q is introduced to address missing markers, where q = 1 + (x/|M| * 2.5), with x being the number of missing markers in a given frame.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Optical marker-based motion capture data from 15 different datasets: ACCAD, BioMotion Lab, CMU, EKUT, Eyes Japan, HumanEva, KIT, MPI HDM05, MPI Limits, MPI MoSh, SFU, SSM, TCD Hand, TotalCapture, and Transitions. Marker sets range from 37 to 91 markers per dataset. The SSM dataset also includes synchronized 4D body scans.
rai:dataImputationProtocol: When there are no markers present on the hands of the recorded subjects, the hand poses are set to the average pose of the MANO model.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: MoSh++ is used to convert mocap marker data into SMPL body model parameters (pose, shape, soft-tissue). The method uses a two-stage fitting process: Stage I estimates body shape and marker locations from randomly chosen frames; Stage II optimizes pose and soft-tissue deformation for each frame. Due to inherent problems with mocap such as swapped and mislabeled markers, results were manually inspected and either corrected or held out.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: MoSh++ maps marker data into SMPL pose, shape, and soft-tissue parameters. The process includes: fitting SMPL-H body model to observed mocap markers, recovering soft-tissue dynamics using DMPL, and solving for hand pose using MANO when hand markers are present. Hyperparameters were tuned using cross-validation on the SSM dataset. A scaling factor b = 46/n is applied to handle varying numbers of markers across datasets. Manual inspection was performed to correct or exclude problematic sequences with swapped or mislabeled markers.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: MoSh++ (extension of MoSh), SMPL body model, SMPL-H (with hand articulation), DMPL (for soft-tissue dynamics), MANO hand model, Chumpy autodifferentiation package, Powell's gradient-based dogleg minimization
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is publicly available at http://amass.is.tue.mpg.de. The authors state they will continuously incorporate more mocap data contributed by themselves and the community, and will support the community in adding new captures as long as they can be similarly shared.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset includes 346 subjects performing various motions. Body shape parameters are captured. Two of the three SSM subjects were professional models who signed modeling contracts allowing release of their 4D scan data.
rai:dataSocialImpact: AMASS enables new applications in animation, visualization, and generating training data for deep learning models of human motion. It can be used to generate synthetic training data for computer vision tasks. The consistent representation makes it useful for a wide range of research applications.
rai:dataLimitations: The source datasets are often narrowly focused on particular classes of motions. The SSM dataset used for hyperparameter tuning used a standard 46-markerset, which may affect generalization to other markersets. Hand articulation evaluation lacks ground-truth data. Current MoSh++ runtime is not real-time.
rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, and Validation of deep learning models for human motion; animation and visualization; generating synthetic training data for computer vision tasks; human pose estimation; body shape reconstruction; soft-tissue dynamics modeling; hand pose estimation.
